page.overview:
Who is Hal Cole?

Hal Cole (born 20 November 1912 and died 12 November 1970) was an American racing driver who participated in the Indianapolis 500 between 1946 and . He result in the 1950 Indianapolis 500 would have counted towards the Formula One championship, but he failed to qualify for the event.

Cole began racing in the 1930s, primarily at dirt tracks. He began competing in the AAA series in 1946, which included the Indianapolis 500. In his first attempt at the race, he suffered a fuel leak early in the race. The following year, he did not participate in the race due to a boycott between the race organizers and the American Society of Professional Auto Racing.

In 1948, he returned to the Indianapolis 500, qualifying 14th. At the end of the 200 laps, he found himself in 6th position, achieving his best finish in the event. The following year, he started 11th, but failed to complete the race distance due to a mechanical issue. His final entry into the race was in 1950, but he failed to qualify.

He died from a heart attack in 1970 at the age of 57.
